strengths: Relevant and timely problem: Extending video diffusion transformers to 'any-reference' multi-subject generation while preventing identity leakage and copy-paste artifacts is an important problem in controllable video synthesis.

Extensive experimental comparisons: The paper compares against a wide range of open-source models (VACE, SkyReels-A2, Phantom, Concat-ID, HunyuanCustom) and proprietary commercial platforms (Kling 1.6, Hailuo, Pika 2.1, Vidu 2.0).

Detailed data curation pipeline: The four-stage pipeline—including cross-pair synthetic data augmentation to avoid rigid spatial overfitting and copy-paste artifacts—is well-engineered and practically useful.
Strong qualitative identity preservation: The visual comparisons and supplementary results show good fidelity across faces, clothing, and multi-subject scenes.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The proposed masked guidance primarily amounts to spatially arranging reference crops onto a single composite canvas and concatenating latents and downsampled binary masks along the channel dimension, which is an incremental variation of existing image-to-video / inpainting conditioning setups. The subject disentanglement module is similarly a straightforward heuristic additive injection.

Mathematical ambiguities and notation errors in Section 3.2: In Equation 6, there is an indexing mismatch between the summation variable $i$ and the mask superscript $k$ ($M_{sub}^k \odot v_i$). Furthermore, $v_i \in \mathbb{R}^D$ is the text value embedding from cross-attention layers, while $z_0 \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times C \times H \times W}$ is the visual latent representation; the paper does not explain the projection mechanism bridging the feature dimension $D$ to the latent channel dimension $C$.

Flawed aggregate metric ('Total Score'): In Tables 1, 2, 3, and 4, the authors compute a 'Total Score' by directly taking the arithmetic mean of metrics with vastly different scales and distributions (e.g., Motion Smoothness $\sim 0.95$, Aesthetic Score $\sim 0.45$, ID-Sim $\sim 0.55$). Such an unweighted arithmetic aggregation is statistically ungrounded and misleading.

Relatively small evaluation benchmark: The quantitative benchmark consists of only 120 reference-text pairs (60 single-ID and 60 multi-subject cases), which is quite small to conclusively evaluate multi-subject composition across diverse entities (humans, animals, clothing, accessories, and backgrounds).

Missing specifics on the exact base backbone: While Wan2.1 is cited throughout, the paper does not clearly specify in Section 3 or Section 4.1 which specific checkpoint (e.g., Wan2.1-1.3B vs. 14B) serves as the base model for MAGREF, making it difficult to fully verify fairness against baselines running Wan2.1-14B.

strengths: Addresses a timely and challenging problem in video generation: any-reference multi-subject generation without cross-subject confusion and copy-paste artifacts.
The proposed masked guidance and composite reference canvas design nicely repurposes pretrained image-to-video capabilities without requiring complex architectural modifications.
The 4-stage data curation pipeline, particularly the cross-pair generative augmentation strategy, directly and effectively targets the prevalent copy-paste bias in reference-conditioned generation.
Comprehensive empirical evaluation covering both single-ID and multi-subject benchmarks, comparing against both open-source methods and proprietary commercial video models.
Extensive ablation studies and qualitative visualizations clearly demonstrate the isolated contribution of each proposed component.
weaknesses: Mathematical and architectural details in the Subject Disentanglement module (Section 3.2, Eq. 6) are underspecified; specifically, the cross-attention value embedding dimension D does not match the VAE latent channel dimension C, and the text-to-latent projection or transformation mechanism before broadcasting is omitted.

The training setup lacks transparency regarding the exact training dataset size (number of video clips/hours) and the exact base model size (e.g., Wan2.1 1.3B vs. 14B), making exact reproducibility difficult.

The evaluation relies on an ad-hoc 'Total Score' computed by simply averaging metrics with completely different underlying scales, distributions, and sensitivities (e.g., ID-Sim, Aesthetic Score, Motion Smoothness).
The benchmark sample size (120 prompt-reference sets in total, with only 60 multi-subject cases) is relatively modest for establishing conclusive benchmark performance in video generation.

strengths: Addresses an important, practical, and challenging problem: any-reference video generation supporting diverse combinations of subjects (humans, garments, accessories, objects, and backgrounds) within a unified framework.

The region-aware masked guidance with pixel-wise channel concatenation provides an effective way to leverage native image-to-video capabilities without requiring intrusive backbone architecture modifications.
The subject disentanglement mechanism provides a simple and effective spatial-semantic binding to prevent identity/attribute leakage across multiple reference subjects.

The four-stage data curation pipeline, particularly the generative cross-pair augmentation, directly targets the pervasive problem of copy-paste / static pose artifacts in reference-conditioned generation.

Extensive experimental evaluation comparing against both modern open-source baselines (e.g., VACE, SkyReels-A2, Phantom) and commercial state-of-the-art systems (e.g., Kling 1.6, Hailuo, Pika 2.1, Vidu 2.0), supported by comprehensive ablations and a human preference study.
weaknesses: Mathematical and technical formulation clarity in Section 3.2: Equation (6) injects text value embedding $v_i \in \mathbb{R}^D$ directly into the latent $z_0 \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times C \times H \times W}$ via element-wise multiplication with mask $M_{sub}^k$, but the paper does not explain how the feature dimension mismatch between text dimension $D$ (typically 1024 to 4096) and VAE latent channel dimension $C$ (typically 16) is bridged (e.g., whether a learnable linear projection is used). In addition, Equation (6) mixes index $k$ in $M_{sub}^k$ with the summation index $i$.

Conceptual novelty is somewhat incremental: combining reference images into a collage/canvas for channel concatenation and applying masked attention / prompt-to-region injection are extensions of established techniques in grounded text-to-image and image-to-video models.

Lack of details regarding the training scale: the paper omits the final size (total video hours/number of clips) of the dataset curated by the four-stage pipeline, as well as the explicit designation of the base diffusion backbone in the main text (e.g., Wan2.1-14B vs. Wan2.1-1.3B).

Metric design: computing the 'Total Score' by directly taking the arithmetic mean of heterogeneous metrics (such as ID-Sim, Subj-Sim, Aesthetic, Motion Smoothness, and GmeScore) is uncalibrated, as these metrics operate on different dynamic ranges and variances.
